topics.title: Head's letter: eight days to go, and who's new this year
topics.summary: Brenda Leaks' first back-to-school letter introduces new faculty and staff: Yara Herman (Lower School art), Helena Rodgers (4th grade lead), Kajsiab Linda Moua (2nd grade, covering a leave), Marcelo Muñoz (Middle School Dean of Students), Hannah Caminos (Spanish), Paula Ciraulo, Russell Wright (drama, grades 3–8), Paul Rendón (5th grade math through winter break), Eliza Cohen (Dean of Service Learning and Field Studies) and Vivian Racz (Development). Three departures over the summer; replacements to be announced in Circle Back.

topics.title: Head's letter: settling in
topics.summary: A reflection on transitions at the start of the year and the Quaker practice of settling in. No dates or actions.

topics.title: Climate survey results published
topics.summary: Results of last year's community climate survey are out. 47% of families responded; the school wants a higher response rate in 2027 and says more requests for feedback are coming.

updates.note: Published, with four more coffee and tea gatherings added for follow-up questions.

topics.title: Head's letter: what is your vision for Friends?
topics.summary: From the coffee gatherings: families value the Quaker grounding, the strength of community, and how well children are known. The most common wish is clarity on the school's direction. Brenda's answer is the mission statement, quoted in full. Families who missed a coffee are asked to answer the same two questions in a short survey.
topics.action: Take the two-question survey if you missed a coffee

topics.title: Coffee & Tea with Brenda (small-group gatherings)
topics.summary: Small-group morning coffees and afternoon teas with the Head of School through September and October. RSVP required; the form lists the dates.

topics.title: Coffee Under the Awning + Community Meeting for Worship
topics.summary: First parent/guardian Community Meeting for Worship of the year, with coffee beforehand.

topics.title: Lower School Back to School Night
topics.summary: Welcome reception and check-in 5:00–6:00 on the yard, program at 6:00 sharp. Childcare registration closed (at capacity).

updates.note: Invitation with the schedule: reception 5:00–6:00, program 6:00, grade-level presentations 6:20–6:50 then classrooms at 7:00, ending about 7:30; check in at the South Valencia gate for a welcome packet and a gift (one per household).
Reminder on the day; childcare full.

topics.title: Middle School Back to School Night
topics.summary: Welcome reception 5:00–6:00 on the yard, program at 6:00. Limited free childcare, first come first served; ED/A3 runs as usual until 6:00.

topics.title: Lower School New Family Check-In
topics.summary: For new Lower School families: routines, cognitive load, and settling in, with the student learning support and counseling teams. RSVP requested.

topics.title: Middle School New Family Check-In
topics.summary: New Middle School parents and guardians: stay after Community Meeting for Worship for coffee and a check-in. RSVP requested.

topics.title: Coffee Under the Awning + Community Meeting for Worship
topics.summary: Coffee at 8:15, then an adults-only Meeting for Worship 8:45–9:15 in the Meeting Room.

topics.title: Coffee Under the Awning + Community Meeting for Worship
topics.summary: Coffee at 8:15, Community Meeting for Worship 8:45–9:15 in the Meeting Room.

topics.title: Kindergarten Ages & Stages
topics.summary: Conversation on social and emotional development for five- to six-year-olds, with Lower School Head Amabelle Sze and Mental Health Specialist Katherine Preston. Moved from Oct 8 to Oct 13; anyone who RSVPed for the old date was asked to RSVP again.

updates.note: NEW DATE: Tue Oct 13. RSVP again.

topics.title: 3rd & 4th Grade Ages & Stages
topics.summary: Conversation on social and emotional development for eight- to ten-year-olds, with Amabelle Sze and Katherine Preston. RSVP requested.

topics.title: 1st & 2nd Grade Ages & Stages
topics.summary: Conversation on social and emotional development, raising children at home and partnering with SFFS, with Amabelle Sze and Katherine Preston. RSVP requested.

updates.note: Direct email from the Lower School Head: the original date was never announced, so the event moved to Mon Nov 2.

topics.title: Middle School Ages & Stages II: Healthy Relationships
topics.summary: How to help middle schoolers navigate shifting friendships, with Katherine Preston and Middle School Counselor Kylie Dayan. On Zoom. RSVP requested.

topics.title: Parenting: Middle School stress and emotional regulation
topics.summary: Middle School Counselor Kylie Dayan and Director of Counseling and Wellness Katherine Preston on adolescent emotional wellness, starting from Dr. Lisa Damour's episode "How to Show Up for Your Teen with Big Emotions". The first of four sessions this year. On Zoom.

topics.title: High School Transition: 8th Grade Parent Coffee
topics.summary: Managing and supporting your teenager (and yourself) through the high school application season, with Kristen Daniel and Katherine Preston. RSVP requested.

topics.title: School Picture Days
topics.summary: Individual photos Oct 19–20, class photos Oct 21. One make-up day only, at the photographer's discretion. The schedule by class and section is published. 8th grade families: avoid booking high school visits on these days. Volunteers were wanted for picture days.

updates.note: Room-parent clerks asked for picture-day volunteers (8 shifts); volunteers must complete the new Mandated Reporter training and a TB questionnaire.
Volunteer sign-up for picture days (both grade digests).

topics.title: Fall Conferences
topics.summary: No school and no enrichment on Oct 29–30. Sign-ups ran in the Family Portal from Oct 19 to noon on Oct 26; after that, contact your child's teacher or advisor. All-day childcare 8am–6pm cost $150 a day by sign-up, free during your own slot. Lower School: teachers share observations, early assessments and work samples and set goals with you (1st grade: 25 minutes, in person, Zoom on request). Middle Schoolers lead their own conferences.

deadline.what: Sign up for a conference slot in the Family Portal

updates.note: Dates and no-school reminder (both grade digests).

How conferences work: Lower School teachers share observations, early assessments and work samples and set goals; Middle Schoolers lead their own. Sign-ups open Oct 19 at 6:00 pm, close Oct 26 at noon. All-day childcare $150/day by sign-up; free during your slot.
Sign-ups open in the Family Portal.
1st grade: 25-minute in-person conferences; email the teachers for Zoom instead.
3rd grade: fill in the pre-conference form by Wed Oct 28.

topics.title: Four-day weekend: no school Oct 9 and Oct 12
topics.summary: Fri Oct 9 is a professional development day; Mon Oct 12 is Indigenous Peoples' Day. No school, no ED, A3 or enrichment either day.

topics.title: GrandFriends Day
topics.summary: Grandparents and special friends visit classrooms. Light refreshments in the Gym, program at 10:00. Register your child's GrandFriend. Added later: Nov 20 is an early dismissal day for all students at 11:30; ED/A3 available, bring a lunch (no ChoiceLunch). Parents can volunteer for the day through a form.

updates.note: Added: early dismissal 11:30 for all; ED/A3 available; no ChoiceLunch.

topics.title: Fall break
topics.summary: No school the week of Thanksgiving.

topics.title: Looking ahead to December
topics.summary: Craft Fair Dec 12, candlelight Meeting for Worship Dec 16, Winter Celebration Dec 18, winter break Dec 21 to Jan 1, first day back Jan 4. All already on Important Dates.

topics.title: SFFS Craft Fair
topics.summary: A festive bazaar of crafts and food made by the community, open to all (invite family and friends), with a Sporting Gear Swap, a 4th grade cafe and a service project assembling hygiene kits with Simply the Basics. Middle Schoolers, parents from every grade, faculty and staff can sell: sign up as a vendor by Fri Dec 4. Middle School vendors must attend training Fri Nov 13 at 11:45 in the Learning Commons.

updates.note: Announced; vendor sign-up open until Dec 4.

topics.title: Middle School Fall Play: Romeo and Juliet—Together [and Alive!] at Last!
topics.summary: A comedy that upends Shakespeare through a middle school production gone wild. Thu Nov 12 and Fri Nov 13 at 7:00, Sat Nov 14 at 1:00 and 5:00. Tickets ($5 youth, $10 adults) went on sale Nov 2 and requests now exceed seating; there are no door sales. The school is looking at more seats and may offer waitlisted families the final dress rehearsal, Wed Nov 11 at 3:00 pm: tell drama teacher Russell Wright (rwright@sffriendsschool.org) if you are on the waitlist and interested. Families who need ticket support can contact him too.

updates.note: Save the date; ticket information coming.
Tickets on sale Mon Nov 2; ticket support available.

topics.title: Emergency alert system test
topics.summary: Test message at 1:00 pm Fri Oct 30 by phone, text and email. All parents are opted in automatically.

updates.note: Direct notice: no action needed; a form to report if you did not get all three messages; the call comes from the school number, do not call back.

topics.title: Annual Fund
topics.summary: Goal $1.2M. Every trustee and administrative leader has given, plus a third of faculty and staff. A class volunteer will be in touch. Latest: 1 in 4 families, closing in on $400,000 (Nov 5).

topics.title: Yard play structure
topics.summary: Reopened after repairs (Oct 29). It had been closed since early October while the school looked at upgrades.

updates.note: Closed while looking at ways to upgrade.
Temporarily closed exploring repairs to make it safer.

topics.title: Candy Monster is back
topics.summary: Bring individually wrapped fun-size Halloween candy to the lobby Nov 2–6 for At The Crossroads, a San Francisco nonprofit working with youth experiencing housing instability. Please keep personal Halloween candy at home; it distracts younger students.

topics.title: Valkyries spirit day
topics.summary: To celebrate the Valkyries' championship, students and staff were invited to wear lavender and black on Wed Nov 4, the day of the parade. School ran as usual, including Middle School MAP testing. Absences needed the Family Portal attendance form by 8:30 am, and missed work must be made up.

updates.note: Announced by the Head of School.

topics.title: Admissions: Open House and school tours
topics.summary: Know a family who might be interested in Friends? Open House was Thu Oct 8; school tours run from Fri Oct 16 through mid-January, registration on Ravenna. Questions to José Zamora (jzamora@sffriendsschool.org) or Chloe Campbell (ccampbell@sffriendsschool.org).

updates.note: Open House Oct 8 and tours announced.

topics.title: Morning carpool traffic safety
topics.summary: Cross Valencia at 14th Street with the crossing guard, never mid-block, and children never alone. Bikes ride with traffic in the bike lane. Avoid turning onto Brosnan Street 8:00–8:30.

topics.title: Parking on the Valencia Street island
topics.summary: You may park or load anywhere on the island including in front of the ramp, but not in the red zone. The white zone is passenger loading (5 minutes) 7:30–8:30 am and 1–6 pm on school days; otherwise 2-hour metered parking. Move your car by 1 pm. Tickets can be contested with SFMTA.

topics.title: Middle School dismissal
topics.summary: Dismissal is 3:15 (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri) and 2:05 on Wednesdays. Students should come down right away when called. Tell your carpool if your student might be in A3, and keep tutoring, enrichment, athletics and rehearsal schedules in mind.

topics.title: Vidigami: the school's photo app
topics.summary: Vidigami is where the school shares classroom, field-trip, athletics and arts photos with families; every family has an account (new families get an invitation email) and students have no access. Grade newsletters link to each grade's album. If the app misbehaves, delete and reinstall it from the App Store or Google Play and log in again.

updates.note: Vidigami is the school's photo-sharing platform; accounts exist for every family, and new families get an invitation email. Students have no access.

topics.title: Donate jigsaw puzzles to the Middle School Learning Commons
topics.summary: Drop unused puzzles at the front desk labelled "LC" or "Jason". A missing piece or two is fine.

topics.title: Let Your Life Speak chalkboard
topics.summary: A large chalkboard rotating around the building poses a question for students, faculty, parents and guests. First question: How will you change the world?

topics.title: Lost and Found
topics.summary: Missing water bottles or clothing? Check the Lost and Found on the first floor near room 118. Unclaimed items are donated over Winter Break.

updates.note: Reminder; items donated over Winter Break.

topics.title: Día de los Muertos altar
topics.summary: The altar, by Spanish teachers Camilo and Mónica and art teacher Yara, is by the front desk; families can add photos of loved ones through a shared Drive folder. 4th graders made Identity Collage Boxes for it. The Spanish food unit ended with salsa and guacamole recipes to make at home.

updates.note: Direct email from the Spanish and art teachers: upload photos of loved ones to a shared folder; 4th graders made Identity Collage Boxes; salsa and guacamole recipes from the Spanish food unit.

topics.title: Horizons at SFFS Future Makers Gala
topics.summary: Fundraiser for Horizons, the summer program for San Francisco public school students that SFFS sponsors. Dancing, food trucks and performances at SOMArts. Result: a record night, almost 200 people and $200,000 raised.

updates.note: Room parents forwarded Horizons' own invitation: early-bird tickets to Sep 1, honoree Katharine Gin, sponsorships available.

topics.title: Fall PGA Kickoff Meeting
topics.summary: Open to all parents and guardians: the work, spirit and needs of the Parent/Guardian Association. Mingle from 4:30, meeting 5:00–6:00, kept to an hour so families can use ED/A3.

topics.title: PGA Service Committee kick-off meeting
topics.summary: Help shape the school's commitment to service and community. Longtime volunteers and newcomers welcome.

topics.title: PGA Equity, Inclusion & Belonging Committee meeting
topics.summary: First EI&B meeting of the year, with Head of School Brenda Leaks on priorities. In person at 260 Valencia or on Zoom.

updates.note: Reminder on the day in both grade digests.

topics.title: An Evening with Betsy Cornwell
topics.summary: Conversation and Q&A with the New York Times bestselling author about her memoir Ring of Salt and her upcoming novel Suffs, co-written with Shaina Taub. RSVP by Sep 25.

updates.note: Reminder in both grade digests (RSVP still open).

topics.title: Spanish-Speaking PGA Committee fall potluck
topics.summary: Music, food, a piñata and good company. Bring a dish for about 8. You don't need to speak Spanish.

topics.title: Mid-Autumn Moon Festival family outing at the Asian Art Museum
topics.summary: Family scavenger hunt hosted by the AAPI Family Affinity Group, then mahjong and mooncakes in Bogart Court. Admission is free on the first Sunday of the month. All families welcome.

topics.title: LGBTQIA+ Affinity Group coffee meet-up
topics.summary: Coffee after drop-off at Four Barrel. A WhatsApp group link is in the email.

topics.title: PGA Jewish Family Affinity Group Sukkot potluck
topics.summary: Kickoff potluck at a host family's home. Bring whoever in your family is available; RSVP and snack sign-up details are in the email.

topics.title: Family affinity and alliance groups
topics.summary: Affinity and alliance groups cultivate belonging: 3rd and 4th graders can join optional adult-led groups once a month at lunch (this year's sign-up closed Oct 2); Middle Schoolers register themselves after a presentation; parents and guardians can join family groups, which run through the PGA Equity, Inclusion & Belonging committee. A list of current groups and an interest form are available.

updates.note: Programme overview from the Director of Community & Belonging: 3rd and 4th graders may join monthly lunchtime groups (sign-up closed Oct 2); Middle Schoolers register themselves; family groups run through the EI&B committee.

topics.title: SFFS Black Families Affinity annual fall dinner
topics.summary: Bring your family for food, drinks and good company; everyone is encouraged to come. Please RSVP so there is enough food (see the email for who to tell).

topics.title: PGA School Store
topics.summary: The store is almost fully online, with the new logo and the FRIENDS collection. A $5 and $10 flash sale of old-logo stock ran Wed Oct 14 on the patio. The committee is also looking for designers to help build the merch line; contact details are in the email.

updates.note: Pop-up at Back to School Nights; designers wanted.

topics.title: Friends Love Spices: limited-edition SFFS tee
topics.summary: A community-testimony shirt designed and printed locally by SFFS parents, in kids' and adult sizes. All proceeds go to tuition assistance. Orders close Nov 1.

topics.title: PGA Mixed-Up Potlucks
topics.summary: Hosts and guests are matched for casual adults-only or family potlucks in November, December and January. Host sign-up closed Oct 14. Guest sign-up: pick up to three dates; closes Nov 1, and matches go out by email after that. Questions to the Mixed-Up Potluck clerk (contact in the email).

topics.summary: Educator and school advisor Eric Hudson on the state of AI in education, early research on how students and teachers use it, and the opportunities and risks ahead. The talk was Nov 2; a recording is available until Dec 4, with resources he recommended.

updates.note: Room-parent clerks forwarded the save-the-date (Mount Tamalpais School, Mill Valley).
Recording available until Dec 4, with recommended resources.

topics.title: Volunteer at the Stay Over Program (Sundays)
topics.summary: Families volunteer 2–4 pm on Sundays at Downtown High School with a family shelter serving SFUSD students, bringing games, crafts and healthy snacks for about 10 people. Sign up for a slot (through December). Questions to friendsatSOP@gmail.com.

topics.title: Holiday card art for teachers and staff
topics.summary: The PGA Teacher and Staff Appreciation committee wants a drawing by a student or parent for the front of this year's winter holiday cards. Send designs to tsa@sffriendsschool.org by Nov 10.

topics.title: Quaker Youth Leadership Program (grades 7–12)
topics.summary: San Francisco Friends Meeting invites 7th to 12th graders to a youth-led Sunday community: Sundays at the Meetinghouse (65 9th Street), some Sundays in Golden Gate Park, four Friday food-sharing service evenings and an October weekend in the Santa Cruz Mountains. Participants earn a certificate. Email children@sfquakers.org.

updates.note: Announced with the full date list.

topics.title: Volunteer with Lower School art

topics.title: Extended Day, enrichment classes and music lessons
topics.summary: Register for enrichment classes and music lessons in Ultracamp; fall classes began the week of Sep 14. Lower Schoolers stay checked into Extended Day during classes (the ED cost is deducted), and any Lower Schooler can drop into ED. Procare tracks ED attendance and invoices; add authorised pick-ups and a payment method there. An ED flat-rate package (7:45–8:05 am and dismissal to 6:00 pm, excluding PD, conference and holiday days) costs $7,350 for the year, with payment plans and adjusted-tuition discounts. Middle Schoolers get After3, athletics, the play and faculty-led activities at no extra cost. Questions to mvendrell@sffriendsschool.org.

updates.note: Registration opens Aug 20 at 7:00 pm; ED flat rate and Procare explained.
Registration open; new classes: Yoga and Mindful Movement (2nd–4th, Mondays) and STEM Fair Club (7th–8th, Wednesdays).

topics.title: Winter enrichment classes and music lessons: registration opens Nov 11
topics.summary: Registration opens Wed Nov 11 at 7:00 pm in Ultracamp; an email with the link goes out then. Classes fill quickly, so create an Ultracamp account beforehand. Classes begin the week of Dec 7. Lower Schoolers stay checked into Extended Day during classes (the ED cost is deducted); Middle Schoolers pay full price. Adjusted-tuition discounts are available. Questions to mvendrell@sffriendsschool.org.

topics.title: Drop-off, pick-up, absences and the weekly dismissal form
topics.summary: Lower School: drop off at the south gate on Valencia; classes start at 8:30 (4th grade 8:20) and late arrivals check in at the front desk. Absence or late arrival: email the teachers and fill in the Attendance Form in the Family Portal. Fill in the weekly Dismissal Form by Sunday evening (only again when plans change); same-day changes, including drop-in ED, go by email to the lead and associate teacher before noon, and after noon also a call to the front desk. Pick up on foot, by bike or through the carpool line with your placard, at the later sibling's time if you have more than one child. Middle School dismissal is 3:15 (2:05 on Wednesdays).

updates.note: Start-of-year procedures from the Lower School Head.
Weekly dismissal form explained; carpool placards mailed.
1st grade teachers: the dismissal form is how they know where to send each child; email both teachers for same-day changes.

topics.title: Snacks, lunch and labelling everything
topics.summary: Every child brings a hearty, healthy snack each day, with a packed lunch or Choicelunch (the lunch delivery program) at midday. Label coats, water bottles and everything else; the Lost and Found is donated regularly.

updates.note: From the Lower School Head's welcome letter.

topics.title: Family Handbook, supply lists and school forms
topics.summary: The 2026–27 Family Handbook is the reference for policies; school forms (including acknowledging it) and Magnus health forms were due Aug 24 through the Family Portal. Supply lists are published by division. Directory preferences and pick-up authorisations live in your Household Profile.

updates.note: Forms due Aug 24; handbook, supply lists and new-family directories.

topics.title: Start of school: class lists, welcome conferences, first day
topics.summary: Class placements were posted in the Family Portal on Aug 19, teachers wrote each child a note, and 15-minute welcome conferences were booked Aug 21–24. The first day, Aug 26, was a half day (dismissal 11:30 K, 11:45 1st–2nd, 12:00 3rd–4th, 12:15 Middle School).

updates.note: Class lists, welcome conference sign-ups, first-day dismissal times.
3rd grade teachers' welcome note: rooms 202 and 205, bring a chapter book.
1st grade teachers' welcome note: meet on the front yard, room 123, pack a snack.

topics.title: How conferences and progress reports work
topics.summary: Lower School: a welcome conference in August, parent conferences in the fall and spring, two progress reports (February and June) and a June Portfolio Celebration where your child shares their work. Middle School: an intake conference, two student-led conferences, two midterm and two formal progress reports, and Presentation Night in spring.

updates.note: Outlined in the Lower School welcome letter.
Explained in full by both division heads before fall conferences.

topics.title: This year's testimony is Community: three queries to talk about at home
topics.summary: Each year the school focuses on one of the SPICES. For 2026–27 it is Community, explored individually, in class and as a school through three queries.
items: What does it mean to be a member of a community?
As a steward of my community, what are the ways I show I care?
What small acts of kindness can make a difference in the world?

updates.note: Announced by the Director of Quaker Life.

topics.title: The new SFFS brand: The future needs Friends
topics.summary: A new visual identity: the tagline The future needs Friends, a quilted-star logo rooted in Quaker textile tradition, and an anthem video. The Fire mascot stays for athletics (it is officially named Fire, blue because blue is the hottest part of a flame). A redesigned website is due next fall for the school's 25th anniversary.

updates.note: Announced by the Director of Communications.

topics.title: Campus safety incident (Sep 11) and the school's response
topics.summary: A bomb threat was phoned to the main line at about 5:50 pm on Fri Sep 11; the few students on campus were evacuated and SFPD searched and cleared the building. No suspect; SFPD does not believe there is an ongoing threat. The school added a second security guard for the week, is reviewing the incident with its security partner, offered counselling support, and held an extra Community Meeting for Worship on Wed Sep 16 at 8:45. A resource on talking with children about violence was shared.

updates.note: Incident reported and resolved the same evening.
Answers to families' questions; extra security; Community MfW Sep 16.

topics.title: Volunteering with students: training and TB check now required
topics.summary: New for 2026 under California Senate Bill 848: volunteers in direct contact with students must complete an online Mandated Reporter training (about 30 minutes, invitation from the school through Vector Solutions) and a TB questionnaire, done at school by Nurse Ann or by your doctor (reimbursed). Questions to Violet Borowski (vborowski@sffriendsschool.org).

updates.note: Explained in the picture-day volunteer request.

topics.title: Room parents: what they do
topics.summary: Each class has two or three room parents (three or four per grade in Middle School), coordinated by the PGA room-parent co-clerks. They support teachers (projects, field-trip sign-ups, communication), build community (potlucks, picnics, Circle of Friends), liaise with the PGA (Blue Party volunteers, teacher appreciation), run class communications (Veracross, email, WhatsApp) and share photos. Your grade's room parents are listed on the class site.

updates.note: Recruiting for 2026–27 with the role description.
3rd grade room parents introduced themselves and asked for 2–3 social coordinators.

topics.title: Circle of Friends: support when a family needs it
topics.summary: A PGA committee that quietly organises help for families through extraordinary events and transitions: a new baby, a move, an illness, a loss. Support can be meals, playdates or carpools. Each class has a Class Friend as liaison; tell them or your teachers if your family, or one you know, could use a hand. Discretion is the rule.

updates.note: 1st grade organised meals and cards for a staff member on medical leave.
The 1st grade Class Friend introduced the role.
1st grade: meal sign-up for a staff member's family after a new baby, Tuesdays and Fridays through Dec 19, delivered to the front desk by 3:00 pm. See the email for the sign-up and dietary notes.

topics.title: Help grow the 1st grade class: admissions asks for your voice
topics.summary: The admissions office wants to grow this class and asked 1st grade families to help: invite friends to tours and the Open House (a last-minute guest only needs a quick email so a name tag is ready), wear school gear, post a review on Niche or in neighbourhood groups, host a casual gathering for prospective families (two hosts wanted), or book 30 minutes to share ideas. Contact José Zamora (jzamora@sffriendsschool.org).

topics.title: A Lower School teacher's leave: Oct 26 to Nov 14 and Jan 4 to 15
topics.summary: Carla is expecting a baby and will be on leave Oct 26 to Nov 14 and again Jan 4 to 15. Annette Palomo, a Middle School associate teacher, covers both windows; the two have planned together all year.

updates.note: Announced by the Lower School Head.

topics.subject: Math
topics.title: Math: Bridges Unit 1, number sense
topics.summary: Counting forward and backward, grouping in 2s, 5s and 10s, and subitizing (seeing 7 as 5 and 2 more) with the rekenrek, a two-row bead frame. The aim is a strong number foundation before addition and subtraction within 20 later in the year.

topics.subject: Literacy
topics.title: Literacy (Fundations): CVC words, sight words, then digraphs
topics.summary: Students are reading and spelling consonant-vowel-consonant words and sentences and learning more high-frequency words. Next: consonant digraphs such as sh, th, ch and wh, which make one sound and get one tap ("shop" has three taps).

updates.note: Finishing Unit 1: lowercase letters, letter sounds, tapping and blending, closed syllables.
CVC words and sentences; digraphs next.

topics.subject: Identity and community
topics.title: Self portraits and Cultural Celebration Shares
topics.summary: The year opened with self portraits (mirror sketches, skin-tone swatches, backgrounds of things each child loves) and read-alouds about skin colour. Now the class is learning about cultures in the community through Hispanic/Latine Heritage Month, Filipino History Month and Indigenous Peoples' Day, and families lead Cultural Celebration Shares; the first was the Mid-Autumn Moon Festival. Sign up to lead a share through the link in the Oct 23 newsletter or the Class Page.

updates.note: Heritage months and the first Cultural Celebration Share.

topics.title: Questions to ask your 1st grader
topics.summary: Conversation starters from the 1st grade teachers. Some children recite their whole day unprompted; most need a nudge.
items: Where do you start the lowercase letters t, b and f?
What sight words (trick words) have you learned so far? Can you spell them?
What is a song or game you learned in class that you can teach me?
With whom do you like to play at recess?
What was your classroom job this week?
Who was the Star of the Week? What did you learn about them?
Have you learned any new songs in Music?
Can you skip count by 5s? By 10s?
Have you ever solved a problem at the Peace Table?

updates.note: First set: who do you play with, your job this week, who you work well with, new connections for a playdate, your 5th grade buddies, a peaceful thought from Meeting for Worship.

topics.title: Star of the Week
topics.summary: Each child gets a week to share something every day except Wednesday: Monday a special object that tells a story (no toys, gadgets or fragile things), Tuesday a special talent (live or a recording emailed to the teachers), Thursday a class interview that becomes a book for their Portfolio box, Friday a school-appropriate song for the Freeze Dance party (send the title to the teachers beforehand). The year's schedule was emailed on Oct 6; teachers also email each family the Friday before, and a day off moves that share to Wednesday.

updates.note: Format explained; schedule to come from the room parents.
Schedule for the whole year, starting the week of Oct 12; swaps via the class WhatsApp.
Teachers will email each family the Friday before their week.

topics.title: 1st grade routines: the red folder, extra clothes, dismissal
topics.summary: Check the red Take-Home Folder in the backpack every week; work, resources and classroom news travel in it. Keep a labelled bag of clean extra clothes at school. Fill in the weekly dismissal form by Sunday evening and email both teachers the morning of any change. Mystery Readers meet the teachers in the lobby so the children are surprised.

updates.note: Red folder, extra clothes, and 1–2 family photos for the classroom (due Sep 11).
Mystery Reader: meet in the lobby.

topics.title: 1st grade team and where things live
topics.summary: Teachers: Nadia Ruiz (nruiz@sffriendsschool.org), Gavin Odabashian (godabashian@sffriendsschool.org) and Olivia Aguirre (oaguirre@sffriendsschool.org). This year includes Morning Meeting, Quiet Time, field trips, and caring for the planet through waste, gardening and tide pools. Photos are on Vidigami; sign-ups are on the Class Page.

updates.note: Welcome letter: what the year holds.
Teacher contacts in the first newsletter.

topics.subject: Math
topics.title: Math: introduction to multiplication
topics.summary: Multiplication through real-world contexts such as grocery stores, postage stamps, tiled patios and baker's trays, to see grouping and repeated addition. Conceptual understanding and efficient grouping come before formal notation. The year also covers division, fractions and geometry.

updates.note: Year overview in the welcome letter.

topics.subject: Social studies
topics.title: Migration, California's native peoples and the Name Project
topics.summary: Social studies explores the cultures of California's native peoples and immigration, with a focus on Chinese migration to San Francisco; trips to Chinatown and Angel Island are planned. The Coyote Hills trip (Oct 8) covered Ohlone life. Every child completed a Name Biography Poster, now displayed across from the music room, and families are sharing migration stories in Migration Shares.

updates.note: Name Project assigned; shares the week of Oct 19.

topics.subject: Spanish
topics.title: Spanish: ordering tacos for real
topics.summary: The food unit ended with a trip on Thu Oct 15 to order tacos in Spanish without a script; each child rehearsed their own dialogue at home (parents were asked to check for allergies). The teachers shared salsa and guacamole recipes afterwards.

updates.note: Menu and each student's dialogue sent home to practise.
Recipes shared with all families (see the Día de los Muertos item).

topics.title: 3rd grade homework: reading and writing
topics.summary: Read independently for at least 30 minutes every night, in a "just right" chapter book (graphic novels do not count): you understand it, get most words right, read smoothly, with expression and with punctuation. Reading aloud to a parent builds confidence. Writing: at least 20 minutes a week in the school/home notebook, about one full page for now, on any topic (prompts are inside the cover); notebooks go home Monday and back Friday. Missed homework is finished on Friday afternoons. Typing Pal is the typing app; home practice is optional (login on the Padlet).

updates.note: 30 minutes of reading nightly; Home/School Book Plan signed and returned Aug 31.
What a good-fit book looks like; writing homework starts.
About one page of writing a week; Typing Pal introduced.

topics.title: 3rd grade routines: chapter books, Morning Meeting, iPads, sharing
topics.summary: Bring one or two chapter books every day (the current one and a backup), never graphic novels. Morning Meeting starts promptly at 8:30, so arrive on time. iPads are used once the signed iPad Expectations agreement is back. In Andrea and Sara's class (3A), each child has an assigned sharing day in Morning Meeting: two minutes, on the week's theme or free share, with photos or short videos uploaded in advance to the class Drive folder; anything brought in must fit in the backpack and stay there.

updates.note: Arrive on time for Morning Meeting.

topics.title: 3rd grade team and where things live
topics.summary: Teachers: Andrea Green (agreen@sffriendsschool.org) and Sara (3A, room 205), Luís Hernandez and Chloe Montoya (room 202), with Stefani Wulkan for learning support (swulkan@sffriendsschool.org). The Padlet holds sign-ups, schedules, Back to School Night slides, homework instructions and the Typing Pal login; photos are on Vidigami; the Learning Support overview is under Resources in the Family Portal.

updates.note: Back to School Night slides and a 3A jobs video on the Padlet.

topics.title: 3rd grade overnight trip: Camp Arroyo, May 3–4, 2027
topics.summary: Two days with WOLF School at Camp Arroyo in Livermore: hiking, campfire and relationship-building away from home, often a first overnight. Packing lists, transport and logistics come closer to the date. Questions to Eliza Cohen, Dean of Service Learning and Field Studies.

topics.subject: Library
topics.title: Library with Suzanne
topics.summary: K–4 classes visit weekly (30 minutes for K, 35 for 1st, 45 for 2nd–4th): a read-aloud with comprehension questions, then browse, choose and check out. Self-selection is the point. Take as many books as you can read in a week or two, return any day, no fines for lost books, and student-written books join the collection. Parents can volunteer; see the PGA library page.

updates.note: Philosophy and a day in the life.

topics.subject: PE
topics.title: Physical Education with Marisa
topics.summary: September built rapport, routines and norms: a jog and dynamic warm-up to start, tag games old and new for locomotor skills, and team-building. 4th graders now have PE in the gym. Contact mhatcher@sffriendsschool.org.

updates.note: Welcome back and what September looked like.

topics.subject: Music
topics.title: Music with Jane
topics.summary: The year opens with "We're Going to Be Friends", sung with Kindergarten, 4th and 8th grade buddies at Meeting for Worship. Community singing is this year's thread: matching pitch, singing with expression, and being part of an ensemble from classroom to grade to whole school. Families are encouraged to sing or listen to music together.

topics.subject: Art
topics.title: Art with Yara
topics.summary: Two studio agreements: Art Can Be Anything, and Mistakes Are Magic. Every class starts with five to ten minutes in a sketchbook. By grade: Kindergarten starts with a single dot and Yayoi Kusama; 1st grade makes recycled-material self portraits; 2nd grade studies Faith Ringgold and makes a paper story quilt about a social issue; 3rd grade studies symbols and logos before designing a personal symbol; 4th grade finishes a collaborative community collage, then an individual cultural-identity collage.

updates.note: New Lower School art specialist, new studio.

topics.title: Questions to ask about art
topics.summary: Open-ended questions from the art teacher for talking about what your child made.
items: Can you tell me about how you made this?
What was a magic mistake you transformed in your art this week?
